status: P30 concept (2026-11-15): low-cost 30x30 aluminium profile chassis with SS400 laser-cut steel plates. Two drive wheels on vertical slide suspension (MISUMI D20 shafts + ball bushings + one spring each), four GL-65 casters bolted rigid. Separate variant; the Rev15 model in cad/layout.json is unchanged.
coordinates: mm; X right, Y forward, Z up, ground Z0. Heading clockwise from +Y (CAD Z rotation = -heading).

frame.section_status: Generic 3030 slot-8 section for display (mouth 8, cavity 16x5.8, core D6.8 = M8 tap drill). Actual supplier section, alloy and end-tap need verification.
frame.inner_rail_note: P30-6 (2026-11-20, user): lower inner rails moved 30 mm inboard (x110 -> 80) so the hub-motor lead leaving the inboard axle end (x131, z90) does not hit the rail; the lead turns up through a grommet hole in the floor

plates.material_note: P30-3: SS400 laser-cut steel, flat (no bending, no welding); thinner than the P30-2 A5052 plates (8/3/5 t) for cost

caster.bolt: M6x8 into M6 tapped corner plate (SS400 6t, 6 mm thread)

bush.supply: Purchase MISUMI long-block linear bushing housing unit, single, standard type (LMU16 inside)
bush.price_seen: 2026-11-18 kr.misumi-ec.com, 1-4 pcs, VAT excl., same-day ship (5+ pcs same price, 14,340 at 1006+)
bush.mount_tap: 2x M6 depth 13 (STEP void D4.8) on the mounting face, pitch 32 along the shaft, first tap 7.5 mm from the housing end
bush.source: MISUMI STEP AP214 (SolidWorks 2016) downloaded 2026-11-18 + catalogue p.249: dr16 D28 L47 L1 32 h27 W36 H49 M6(13), C 775 N, C0 1180 N, 204 g

spring.source: MISUMI SWU21-70 catalogue 2026-11-18 (non-economy SWU, MOQ 1, 7,290 KRW ex VAT, stock 137): OD21 ID13.5 L70 5.37 N/mm, allowable deflection 42, load 225.6 N. Wire section 3.75x1.875 measured on the supplied STEP; solid height assumed 28 (= L - allowable deflection); display turns estimated from the STEP volume (drawing only)

shaft.price_seen: 2026-11-18 kr.misumi-ec.com, 1-4 pcs, VAT excl. (5-19 pcs 8,316), ships day 2-5
shaft.source: MISUMI STEP AP214 downloaded 2026-11-18 (L124, M6 both ends, g6, induction hardened 58HRC)

drive.housing_center_z_note: P30-5 (2026-11-18): the LHSS16 housing bottom (centre + 23.5) sits 10.05 mm above the tip of the droop stoppers on the lower holder (holder top 125 + C-USLH10 17 = 142); contact at -10 with 0.05 mm gap

droop_stopper.note: 2 per wheel on the lower holders (one under each housing, y = +-guide_y), tip up; x161 keeps the tip on the solid part of the LHSS16 bottom (checked in build); M5 tap through the 6t holder, thread end hangs free over the stub-side gap (holder inner part is cantilevered, x<190)

drive.wheel_mount: P30-4 (2026-11-18, user choice A): one flat SS400 10t axle plate per wheel, vertical (YZ), no bend and no plate-to-plate joint in the load path. Motor axle clamped on its face (D-hole AF10.2, spacer + washer + M14 nut). Two MISUMI LHSS16 housed ball bushings bolted to its outer face (2x M6 each from the inner face) ride the guide shafts, so the plate (and the wheel axle normal to it) is set parallel to the shafts by the machined housing faces. A flat 6t spring seat sits on the plate top edge (2x M6).
drive.spring_x_note: Spring stud between the shafts (x179) and the motor side; P30-5: no washer or nut above the upper holder any more

motor_cable.note: P30-6: hub-motor lead (320 mm) leaves the inboard axle end at x131 z90, runs under the floor between the moved inner rail (x65..95) and the axle plate (x142) to a D25 floor hole at y-130 (clear of the battery bridge feet), then to the driver -Y end; the LEFT lead must cross to the right-side driver (likely needs an extension), split grommet D16 bore

electronics.status: Battery, LCD and speaker from company STEP files. Controller, computer, drivers, power distribution are envelopes; DC/DC DDR-240B-24 is a size reservation.

motor_driver.electrical: Input 20-48 VDC (typ. 36), output current 15 A typical / 30 A peak per channel, over-voltage 60 V, under-voltage 16 V; hall U/V/W + incremental encoder A/B inputs, 5 V supply to encoder and hall; CANopen (CiA301/402, 25-1000 kbps) and RS485 Modbus-RTU; 2 programmable opto inputs; 0-50 C
motor_driver.source: ZLAC8015D Servo Driver Manual (Special for Hub Servo Motor) V1.0, ZLTECH (www.zlingkj.com): 2.1 electrical index, 2.2 environment, Fig.1 installation dimension 168 x 89 x 29.7 (body 158, side hole pitch 42). Corner-hole pitch not dimensioned in the figure (envelope only)
motor_driver.fit_to_motor: ZLLG65ASM250-N V2: 24 V, 10 A rated / 30 A stall, 1024-line magnetic A/B encoder + hall. ZLTECH lists ZLAC8015/ZLAC8015D as the driver for its 6.5-inch hub servo motors; 7S pack 21-29.4 V is inside 20-48 V. Confirm the encoder connector (motor single-ended A/B vs driver iA+/iA-) with ZLTECH before ordering
motor_driver.mount: On edge (narrow side down, manual-recommended for heat) beside the battery; heatsink face on a 3t SPCC L-bracket (4x M3x10 through the ears, thermal pad), bracket foot 2x M5 through the floor with nuts underneath

electronics.driver_note: driver_x/driver_size were the P30-1..5 twin-driver envelopes; P30-5b uses one ZLAC8015D (motor_driver)
electronics.print_note: P30-5b: LCD and speaker holders 3D-printed (PETG/ASA, 5 mm plate, 6 mm foot, ribs); grounding by cable to an M4 ground stud

battery_clamp.note: P30-7 (user: one direction was free with the bridges): one printed clamp per battery END (Y faces: wall = Y, lip = Z, corner cleats on the X faces = X); 2x M5 from above per clamp, nuts under the floor; foot limited to x+-60 (PCB standoffs at x69.5/-79.5)

electronics.pcb_note: P30-7: controller PCB + computer moved 16 mm forward (y200 -> 216) so the front battery clamp bolts are not under the PCB

sensors.camera_fov_note: Depth FOV H58.4 x V45.5 (cad/parts.json + Rev15 viewer). Optics x = the three front openings of the Astra STEP (lens barrel D13.3, centre lens D17, window 21.8x14.5) in the camera frame; which one is the depth camera is not identified, so all three are checked
sensors.camera_yaw_note: P30-3: outward yaw 15 -> 5 deg. At 15 deg the outer optic of the left camera saw the front-left TiM571 (7.9% of the image, nearest 29 mm); clear from 6 deg down. Combined horizontal view +-34.2 deg (was +-44.2); the LiDARs cover the sides
sensors.lidar_mount_note: P30-6: TiM571 on an 8 mm printed base: 2x M3 countersunk from below into the scanner (spacing assumed), then 3x M5 from above on the inboard tongue through the 2t floor, nuts underneath. Scan plane Z206.83 (Rev17 matched to it)

lidar_base.note: P30-6 (user): LiDAR fixed to the body plate only. Local frame: +Y = heading. The tongue (local Y -38..-62) lies in the blind sector, inside the frame corner (no rail below), so the three M5 nuts sit under the floor and the bolts stay reachable from above with the scanner mounted

camera_mount.note: P30-7 (user: re-check the camera fixing): the 3.5 mm flange under the rail + leg + shelf + a LOOSE wedge (it had no fixing) were replaced by one print: 7 mm upright plate on the rear face of the top front rail (2x M5 horizontal into rear-slot T-nuts at z270) + yawed web + back plate with the 2 camera M2 + rear ledge

load_case.note: Same design mass as Rev15 (20 kg arm included). Simple static estimates only.
